terms.comment: “Whose is it?” is Cujus est?; “it’s mine”, meum est (Hor. Ep. 1.16.35). The owner is dominus. “Belong to” is usually the genitive of the owner with esse: Aegōnis est, “it belongs to Aegon”; the question is cujum?, “whose?” (Verg. Ecl. 3.1). For belonging to a group, see member.

phrases.latin: omnia possideat, nōn possidet āëra Mīnōs
phrases.english: Minos may own everything, but he doesn’t own the air

phrases.latin: Dīc mihi, Dāmoeta, cujum pecus, an Meliboeī? — Nōn, vērum Aegōnis; nūper mihi trādidit Aegōn.
phrases.english: Tell me, Damoetas, whose flock is that? Meliboeus’s? — No, it’s Aegon’s; Aegon handed it over to me the other day.
